newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MITI panel calls for corporate bond reforms.
newsitem.headline: Japan MITI panel calls for corporate bond reforms.

text.p: Japan should reform its primary corporate bond market by promoting competition among underwriters, a subcommittee under the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said on Thursday.
Compared with the euro primary bond market, the domestic market is less attractive for issuers due to higher underwriting fees, the subcommittee for industrial finance said in a statement.

"Competition among financial institutions should be promoted so that corporations can enjoy low-cost services in the domestic primary bond market that match those offered in the euro market," the statement said.
The subcommittee, made up of 19 members including academics, company directors and economists, plans to finalise its financial reform proposals by early June.
